newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL NBA-TIMBERWOLVES SIGN AUSTRALIAN HEAL, LITHUANIAN PRASKEVICIUS.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL NBA-TIMBERWOLVES SIGN AUSTRALIAN HEAL, LITHUANIAN PRASKEVICIUS.

text.p: The Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday went international, signing Australian guard Shane Heal, Lithuanian forward Virginius Praskevicius and centre Dean Garrett, who played the last two seasons in Greece.
All three got one-year deals, the club announced.

The six-foot (1.83 metres) Heal, who attracted attention for a feisty spirit but not for good judgment when he tussled with burly Charles Barkley this summer, played on Australia's 1992 and 1996 Olympic teams and 1994 world championships team.

In an exhibition game against Dream Team III ahead of the Atlanta Olympics, Heal sank eight three-pointers and scored 28 points against the Americans and got involved in a shoving match with Barkley, who later praised Heal's play.
The Timberwolves invited Heal to their Summer Showcase League, where he averaged six points per game in three contests.
Heal currently is averaging a team-high 24.9 points for Sydney of the National Basketball League in Australia and is shooting 49 percent from three-point range, tops in the league.
He was NBL Rookie of the Year in 1988 and earned first-league honours in 1991 and 1994.

Praskevicius played for Atletas of the Lithuanian League and averaged 14.7 points and 8.5 rebounds in 32 games. In five playoff games, the 6-foot-8 (2.03 metres) Praskevicius averaged 20.6 points on 66 percent shooting.
He averaged 12 points and shot 66.8 percent from the field in the Summer Showcase League.
The 6-11 (2.11 metres) Garrett, a former Indiana University star, spent the last season with PAOK in Greece, averaging 10.6 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game.

Garrett, who was part of Indiana's U.S. collegiate championship team in 1987, played six seasons in Italy. He originally was a 1988 second-round draft pick of the Phoenix Suns, who waived him prior to the 1988-89 season.
